raw_record.question_text: Triangle RZT is generated by rotating the equilateral triangle AZC about point Z. Angle $\beta=\angle \mathrm{CZR}=70^{\circ}$. Determine angle $\alpha=\angle \mathrm{CAR}$.

method.method_draft: Angle-chase using the rotated copy and an isosceles triangle. From the image, note that A, Z, C form the left equilateral triangle, R is the upper vertex of the rotated triangle, and the dashed segment AR is the line forming alpha with AC. From the text, triangle RZT is the rotation of equilateral triangle AZC about Z, so A maps to R and therefore ZA = ZR. Also, since AZC is equilateral, angle AZC = 60°. The image/text give beta = angle CZR = 70°, with ray ZC between ZA and ZR, so angle AZR = 60° + 70° = 130°. In isosceles triangle AZR, the base angles are (180° - 130°)/2 = 25°, so angle ZAR = 25°. At A, the equilateral triangle gives angle CAZ = 60°. Therefore alpha = angle CAR = angle CAZ - angle RAZ = 60° - 25° = 35°.

推理：因为三角形 RZT 是等边三角形 AZC 绕点 Z 旋转得到的，所以 A 旋转到 R，旋转保持距离，因此 ZA=ZR。又因为 AZC 是等边三角形，所以 ∠AZC=60°。已知 ∠CZR=70°，且 ZC 在 ZA 与 ZR 之间，所以 ∠AZR=∠AZC+∠CZR=60°+70°=130°。在三角形 AZR 中，ZA=ZR，因此它是等腰三角形，底角相等，所以 ∠ZAR=(180°−130°)/2=25°。在 A 点，等边三角形给出 ∠CAZ=60°。虚线 AR 位于 ∠CAZ 内，所以 α=∠CAR=∠CAZ−∠RAZ=60°−25°=35°。

method.method_draft: Coordinate/chord-direction method. From the image, use the relative order of rays around Z: take ray ZA as direction 0°, ray ZC as direction 60° because AZC is equilateral, and ray ZR as direction 130° because angle CZR = 70° beyond ZC. From the text, the rotation sends A to R, so ZA = ZR; scale the common length to 1. Place Z at the origin with A = (1,0), C = (cos 60°, sin 60°), and R = (cos 130°, sin 130°). Then AC is a side of the equilateral triangle, so the direction of vector AC from A is 120°. The chord AR joining points on the unit circle at central angles 0° and 130° has direction (0°+130°)/2 + 90° = 155° from A to R. Therefore the angle between AC and AR is 155° - 120° = 35°.
